transcript.text: Alright, let's get this coordination meeting started. We've got tomorrow's inbound delivery — one palletized lot of generator housings and one lot of communications cable reels — and I need to publish final lane assignments before everyone leaves today. The draft plan currently treats all three staging lanes as interchangeable with no special receiving controls listed. Before I lock in assignments, I need to hear from each of you: warehouse ops NCO, movement control officer — are there any changes or issues affecting tomorrow's receiving plan that I need to know about?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Sir, there's a critical issue you need to know before locking in lane assignments. I confirmed this morning that only Lane 2 has a current floor-load certification for the 1,800-kilogram generator-housing pallet. The certification is filed in the warehouse binder, but it hasn't been added to the yard diagram yet — which is why the draft plan still shows all three lanes as interchangeable. The generator-housing pallet must go to Lane 2; Lanes 1 and 3 are not certified for that weight.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Sir, I need to flag a critical issue as well. I received the carrier's vehicle diagram this afternoon and confirmed that the cable-reel tilt-bed requires a 4.0-meter turning clearance that is only available at Lane 3. This diagram hasn't been included in the movement-control brief yet, which is another reason the draft plan still treats all lanes as interchangeable. The cable-reel delivery must be assigned to Lane 3 — no other lane provides the required turning clearance for that vehicle.
